transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-24
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nora Kim (Redwood CSM) / Lina Morales (Nexus CTO), Jordan Lee (Network), Priya Desai (Security), Mark Rivers (SRE)

Summary: quick discovery on Private / VPC deployment, network topology options, region constraints, security controls, and benchmarking requirements.

00:00 Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm avery from Redwood, we've got samir our se and nora on the call, hows everyone?
00:32 Lina Morales: hi all, lina here, yes thanks for making time, we're evaluating private deployments for telecom workloads, latency is important and also we need to keep everything in eu-west-1 for awhile.
00:50 Samir Patel: great, quick intro: Redwood Private can run in your VPC, we support multiple connectivity options — standard VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (private endpoints), and we can also work with Transit Gateway for hub-and-spoke. there's tradeoffs on cross-account peering and egress paths.
01:18 Jordan Lee: when you say private endpoint, is that the same as PrivateLink? we currently have a DirectConnect and want to avoid exposing anything to public internet.
01:35 Samir Patel: yes PrivateLink is AWS' private endpoint option; we can expose service endpoints into your account so traffic never transits the public net. VPC peering is simpler but has scale and transitive limitations; Transit GW solves transitive but has cost.
02:10 Priya Desai: security question - what about KMS and HSM? we need customer-managed keys and full audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
02:28 Avery Chen: understood. we support customer KMS integration and can do HSM-backed keys via your KMS/HSM. audit logs and access logs can be forwarded to your splunk/elk via our logging export or pulled from the private control plane. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs.
03:05 Mark Rivers: any compliance issues if we keep data egress in eu-west-1 but have control plane possibly in us-east? we need data residency guarantees.
03:22 Samir Patel: good point — we offer two patterns: one is private control plane with control messages across regions (we'd document flow), second is fully private control plane in customer VPC / on-prem where nothing leaves. for most telecom customers we can pin both control and data region to eu-west-1 under Private deployment.
03:50 Jordan Lee: what about peering across accounts? our infra accounts are separate, and we use cross-account peering with shared transit gateway.
04:08 Samir Patel: we do support cross-account peering; common approaches: 1) Redwood VPC peered into your infra account(s) 2) PrivateLink endpoints created in your account connecting to Redwood services 3) we deploy into your account (customer-managed Private) if you want full isolation. each has different IAM and routing setup.
04:42 Lina Morales: latency numbers? our target is sub-50ms p99 for core inference calls over direct connect where possible.
04:58 Samir Patel: ok for sequence lengths in telecom workflows what's typical? you mentioned short sequences but high qps?
05:12 Lina Morales: mostly small prompts, median seq ~128 tokens, spikes to 512 during edge cases. qps target initially 200 rps, burst to 1k for events.
05:30 Samir Patel: that maps well — our runtime can do batching; for Private we'll size dedicated pools. we'll likely recommend a mix: dedicated GPU pool in eu-west-1 with autoscale and a small hosted fallback in other region for DR.
06:05 Avery Chen: cost tradeoffs: Dedicated reserved capacity vs fully private on-customer account — dedicated gives us predictable throughput with Redwood-managed infra; private in your account gives max isolation but shifts ops to you. the pricing will reflect that.
06:35 Jordan Lee: network egress — will there be NAT or egress to internet for model downloads/updates?
06:48 Samir Patel: model artifacts and image pulls can be staged to a private S3 in your account or via signed, ephemeral URLs over a secured channel. we can avoid public egress by using S3 endpoints and your ECR repositories.
07:15 Priya Desai: how do you handle secrets and key rotation?
07:25 Avery Chen: we integrate with your KMS for key wrapping, and we can rotate service-level keys periodically. we also support HSM if you require FIPS 140-2 style hardware.
07:50 Mark Rivers: are there firewall requirements or specific security groups/ports?
08:00 Samir Patel: mostly HTTPS/TLS on private endpoints, and some internal control plane ports for health checks. we'll send a minimal inbound/outbound port list.
08:22 Jordan Lee: about routing — can we route via our Transit Gateway so all peering is centrally managed?
08:33 Samir Patel: yes Transit GW is supported; it's our recommended when you have many accounts/nets. note, Transit GW can add a little latency but simplifies management.
08:55 Lina Morales: region constraints again — primary eu-west-1, but we'd like a warm standby in us-east-1. can you replicate KV cache across regions?
09:12 Samir Patel: cross-region KV cache replication is non-trivial. we don't replicate live KV cache across regions for low latency; we instead rely on model variants deployed in target region and fallback routing. warm standby with cross-region async state sync is possible but will increase complexity.
09:45 Avery Chen: we can architect a fallback: eu-west-1 primary, with us-east-1 cold/warm pool that takes over on failover; for session affinity you'd need sticky routing or prefix caching shared via your storage. we'll detail options.
10:10 Mark Rivers: any prior telecom customers done this?
10:18 Samir Patel: yes a couple of carriers ran private deployments with Transit GW + Dedicated pools; we have a redwood case study we can share, though I might have the company name slightly off in my head.
10:40 Nora Kim: i'll add the case study link in the follow-up, plus the security pack.
11:00 Jordan Lee: what's the onboarding timeline — from contract to first inference in prod?
11:12 Avery Chen: typical is 6-12 weeks: infra setup, peering / PrivateLink, KMS integration, model onboarding and benchmarking, then a pilot. committed Dedicated customers who want aggressive timelines can compress that.
11:40 Priya Desai: will we get log-level access for audits?
11:47 Samir Patel: yes, audit logs and token-level traces can be exported; we'll work with your SIEM team to ship logs to your account or a secure S3 bucket.
12:10 Lina Morales: network egress costs — if we use PrivateLink vs peering, there are price differences, right?
12:20 Samir Patel: correct, PrivateLink has endpoint hourly costs and data processing charges. VPC peering is simpler but no endpoint charge. Transit GW has attachments charges and data processing also. we'll provide an estimate in the cost comparison.
13:00 Mark Rivers: do you do canary deploys for model changes in Private?
13:07 Samir Patel: yes, rollouts are supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback. even in Private we manage rollouts via the Redwood control plane or a customer-managed control plane if you choose the fully private deploy.
13:40 Jordan Lee: curious about kernel/quantization — we run int8 for inference, any gotchas?
13:50 Samir Patel: we have quantization profiles and kernel selection; some models behave differently at low bit rates — we'll recommend test prompts and evaluation harnesses.
14:20 Lina Morales: ok next steps from our side: share CIDR ranges, account IDs, and a list of stakeholders and SLAs.
14:35 Avery Chen: noted — from our side we'll send the peering diagrams, security docs, and a preliminary pricing sheet.
15:00 [...call continues with deeper technical Q&A, transcript condensed...]
20:12 Jordan Lee: about private endpoints — we have strict NACLs, will that require any special config?
20:20 Samir Patel: we can work within NACL constraints; endpoints are just ENIs in your subnet in the PrivateLink case. you control the subnet and NACL, so you can lock down to specific ports.
24:00 Priya Desai: can you integrate with our SSO (SAML) and RBAC?
24:10 Avery Chen: yes, SSO via SAML/SCIM and RBAC is supported; we'll map roles to Redwood console permissions.
28:30 Mark Rivers: any hard minimum on commit for Dedicated?
28:40 Avery Chen: typically reserved capacity contracts have monthly/annual commits — we'll show a few tiers. Dedicated is recommended for predictability at scale.
33:00 Samir Patel: for benchmarking, we'll need a small test harness: an account or peered endpoint, a sample model, and a controlled qps ramp. we can run token-level tracing to measure p50/p95/p99 latency.
36:12 Lina Morales: are there network tests you run?
36:20 Samir Patel: yes we do basic iperf-like checks, and synthetic inference traffic with pinned prompts to estimate batching and tail latencies.
40:05 Jordan Lee: any constraints on EBS or storage types for model cache?
40:12 Samir Patel: we recommend NVMe-backed ephemeral for local cache for best throughput; we can also pull from EFS or S3 depending on persistence needs. we'll include a recommended infra spec.
44:50 Priya Desai: data retention - can you guarantee deletion windows?
45:00 Avery Chen: yes, we support configurable retention and can set automatic purges; for Private deployments data never leaves your account unless explicitly configured.
48:30 Mark Rivers: what's required to run the first benchmark next week?
48:40 Samir Patel: we need the CIDR ranges, account IDs, route table info, and a set of representative prompts + expected qps ramp. we'll schedule a 90-minute deep dive to run the tests.
50:05 Lina Morales: timeline - we'd like a pilot within 3 weeks if possible.
50:12 Avery Chen: sounds doable; we'll aim to get the infra prepped in 1 week after we get CIDR and accounts, then benchmark and pilot in week 2-3.
52:00 Nora Kim: i'll coordinate calendaring and share the follow-up items.
54:20 Avery Chen: recap / next steps - we'll send peering diagrams, security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS HSM notes), preliminary pricing, and propose a date for the networking deep dive. Jordan to send CIDRs and account IDs.
55:00 Jordan Lee: ok I'll gather the info and send it to avery and nora.
56:10 Priya Desai: one last question — can you support FIPS/HSM for production keys?
56:20 Samir Patel: yes we support HSM-backed KMS; we'll include details in the security doc.
57:05 Avery Chen: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week. bye.
57:43 call ended
